Retrieve the scalar intensity of the current sample, $s_i$.
Retrieve the scalar intensity of the previous sample, $s_{i-1}$.
Compute the modulation factor $\beta$ using the piecewise function defined below.
*   $s_i$ is the scalar intensity of the incoming sample.
*   $s_{i-1}$ is the scalar intensity of the previous sample along the viewing ray.
*   **Precision:** If the scalar intensity range is large (e.g., 0-255 or 0-65535), the difference $s_i - s_{i-1}$ may exceed 1, causing $\beta$ to become negative.
*   **Degenerate input:** If $s_i = s_{i-1}$, $\beta = 1$, meaning no modulation occurs.
Use when scalar intensity differences are more relevant than gradient changes for identifying features.
It is used in volume rendering to enhance the visibility of internal structures by modulating accumulated transparency based on scalar intensity changes.
